newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's National, Labour agree to pension referendum.
newsitem.headline: NZ's National, Labour agree to pension referendum.

text.p: National and Labour have agreed to hold a referendum on compulsory superannuation as part of a coalition deal with New Zealand First, the New Zealand Herald reported on Friday.
The paper said it understood National's decision to defer the July 1 tax cuts was related to the referendum offer.
New Zealand First wants the cuts to coincide with the introduction of its compulsory savings programme to cushion the impact on taxpayers' pockets.
"National has apparently persuaded it that it is not feasible to have the savings system ready by July 1, so New Zealand First wants the tax cuts deferred too," the Herald said.
The paper said there was dissent among MPs at National's caucus on Wednesday, led by Whangarei MP John Banks.
Banks said on Thursday he would have no part of any plan to delay the promised tax cuts.
